gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only lab measurement of the Anycubic Kobra S1 (igor'sLAB, Tim Kutzner, April 2025) read 59.6 dB(A) while printing, about 15.6 dB above the ≤44 dB quiet-mode claim that ChatGPT used to rank it quietest. The same tester measured the Bambu P1S at 64.7 dB(A) from 40 cm, while Notebookcheck measured the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 at a 44–47 dB average.
standout_why: Product Bible (cited) ranks the enclosed printers only by makers' own figures, Kobra S1 ≤44/≤46 dB, and says so. 3D Printer World (cited) gives the CC2's 44–47 dB with 54 dB peaks and P2S figures of 54/58 dB as 'measured result' but names no tester, distance or date (the CC2 numbers match Notebookcheck's review). StarterBench (cited) gives 3D Printed Decor's 72 dB for the P1S and 65 dB for the P2S without distance or conditions. Additive Realm (rank 5–6) has no dB figure for any of these enclosed printers, only a Prusa owner's forum test. None of these pages has any independent measurement of the Kobra S1. None names igor'sLAB, and none puts a named tester and date next to each figure.
decides: It overturns ChatGPT's pick. Its #1 'quietest' printer, the Kobra S1, rests only on Anycubic's ≤44 dB claim, and the one named lab reading is 59.6 dB(A), close to the 64.7 dB(A) the same tester got for the P1S that ChatGPT advised against. The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 then has the lowest named measurement: Notebookcheck read a 44–47 dB average with 54 dB peaks. Different testers and unstated distances mean the CC2 vs Kobra S1 gap is indicative, not exact, but the measured evidence favors the CC2 for an apartment. The Flashforge Adventurer 5M Pro, which Dealectric lists (claimed 50 dB low-noise mode), has no independent measurement. igor'sLAB's 62.3 dB(A) applies to the non-Pro 5M, with the noise blamed on the 3010 hotend fan, which does not support a quiet pitch for the Pro.

findings.label: Measured noise while printing (igor'sLAB, Tim Kutzner)
findings.source_title: Anycubic Kobra S1 Combo im Test – Zusammenfassung und Fazit (igor'sLAB)
findings.note: Published 2025-04-14. The page says 'im Betrieb' (in operation) and reports no fans audible at idle. It gives no distance or print mode; igor'sLAB's other printer tests state about 40 cm from the closed front. The reading is 15.6 dB above Anycubic's ≤44 dB quiet-mode claim (59.6 − 44) and 13.6 dB above its ≤46 dB standard-mode claim. The same page lists power draw of 180 W printing PLA.

unsourced: A named measurement of the Prusa CORE One: Tom's Hardware's review returned 403 through r.jina.ai and the direct fetch was truncated, and no dB value was readable. 3D Printer World gives 55–61 dB full speed and 52–58 dB stealth for the first CORE One without naming a tester.

A named measurement of the Bambu Lab H2S, the P2S from a lab with a stated distance, or QIDI Q1 Pro / Q2 / Plus4: none was found in the Notebookcheck or igor'sLAB searches. The Notebookcheck X2D and Creality K2 Combo reviews contain no dB figures.
An independent measurement of the Flashforge Adventurer 5M Pro: Tom's Hardware and Anton Mansson mention noise only qualitatively.
A Kobra S1 quiet-mode reading and the distance for igor'sLAB's 59.6 dB(A): the page states neither.
Prices: out of scope for this angle and not checked.
